failure_summary.description: At least one explicit requested outcome was omitted or left unmet by a call for a different operation.
Endpoints were chosen by topical similarity or treated as substitutes despite differing in their documented operation or output.
Calls omitted required fields, misplaced parameters, used unsupported values, or supplied an argument in the wrong form.
Calls were added for unrequested or redundant operations, including endpoints suggested only by topic overlap.

patch.reasoning: The most prevalent problem is treating a related call as coverage for a distinct requested result. An endpoint-level coverage test can help prevent both omissions and topical substitutions, while requiring every emitted call to map to an explicit outcome helps limit extras. Existing schema guidance already addresses parameter and type errors, so it is not repeated here.

edits.target: - Choose an endpoint by its documented operation, output, target, and support for the requested qualifiers—not merely by a shared topic or entity name. Prefer the most specific endpoint that fits the request; use separate endpoints when distinct deliverables require them.
edits.content: - Use the endpoint-level contract (operation and fields), not provider-level marketing text, to decide what a call covers. A requested output is covered only if that endpoint explicitly returns it with the requested qualifiers; calls about the same entity do not imply coverage of other outputs, and every emitted call must map to an explicit requested outcome.
